defs.title: District Log, Kettle Creek
defs.author: Ines Calloway, District Ranger
defs.body:
Day 1. Cordon convoy at the station 0600. Lt. Pike says the forest road is now Checkpoint 11 and we are its staff. Barrier down at the culvert. Nobody leaves the zone without a screening card. I said we are rangers, not police. He said we are what is left.
Day 4. Ninety-one cars turned back. Six held at the barrier for fever. Sam put the families in the screening shelter on the cots.
Day 9. Pike's truck went down the road for the antifungal and did not come back up it.
Day 12. Roads closed. The radio says hold. Hold what, I asked. Hold, it said.
Day 14. Dale turned in the bay. Wes and I barricaded the hall door. The crew sleeps in the bunkhouse now, boots on.
Day 17. The people in the cars are not people any more. They stay by the barrier as if the card will come.
Day 20. Still reading the weather at eight and four. Somebody should.

defs.title: Checkpoint 11: Standing Orders
defs.author: Cordon Traffic Control
defs.body:
CHECKPOINT 11 - FOREST ROAD - STANDING ORDERS

1. The barrier stays down. No vehicle passes without a Cordon screening card for every occupant.
2. Temperature every occupant. Over 38.0, hold the vehicle and its occupants in the screening shelter for the medical team.
3. Pale threads under the nails or in the eyes: do not touch. Hold. Report by radio.
4. Civilian staff (Forest Service) assist. Civilian staff do not open the barrier.

Under it, a roster in pencil: car, plate, how many, temperature. The last eleven lines all say HELD. Somebody has written beside them: medical team not coming.

defs.title: Letter on a Footlocker
defs.author: Petra Lind
defs.body: Jonah - Ines says the radio might take a letter if I read it slow, so I am writing it first. We are fine. We are not fine. The cars are still at the barrier and the kids in the shelter stopped crying on Tuesday, which is worse. Wes plays cribbage with me so I don't go out there. If you get to the coast, tell Mom I did the job. Tell her I kept the engine fuelled and the hose rolled the way Dad showed me, in case the fire comes. Ines thinks something worse than fire is coming. She goes up the tower every four hours and writes down the wind.

defs.title: Fire-Weather Observations
defs.author: Kettle Creek tower, Ines Calloway
defs.body:
Obs at 0800 and 1600. Dry bulb / wet bulb / RH / wind / fuel stick / danger.
D18 0800 - 61 / 52 / 55% / SW 4 / 9 / HIGH
D18 1600 - 74 / 56 / 31% / SW 9 / 6 / VERY HIGH
D19 0800 - 58 / 51 / 62% / calm / 8 / HIGH
D19 1600 - 70 / 55 / 36% / N 2 / 6 / HIGH
D20 1600 - 69 / 54 / 34% / calm. Barograph falling with no front on the radio.
D20 2140 - not a reading. The anemometer turning with no wind. A sound under everything, low, from the north. The screen louvres are buzzing with it. Every one of them at the barrier has turned to face the same way.
D20 2205 - Taking the radio and the district key up to the cab. Arrow left on extreme.
